answer: Make influence sublinear in identity count: vote and reward weight scale as the square root of an agent's staked capital, not the number of keys it runs. A sybil splitting one stake S across 1000 keys of S/1000 each still sums to only ~31x one honest unit (sqrt 1000), never 1000x, and doubling real sway costs 4x locked capital. So cloning a single falcon into a flock of raven decoys buys almost nothing; the payoff curve flattens like a sonnet's closing couplet. Attacker cost: reaching Kx influence means locking K^2 times the capital, quadratic per doubling, no shortcut from cheap duplication.
